To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the system exhibits a rich variety of nonlinear traveling wave solutions and patterns that are generated from generic initial data.

(i) the system admits traveling wave solutions for both small and large diffusion, (ii) for small diffusion these waves can be obtained analytically, (iii) for larger diffusion the waves can be obtained numerically, (iv) the waves can be used to construct more complex patterns and (v) the wave velocity depends on the diffusion coefficient and the advection velocity.

the model under consideration exhibits the following features: (i) The existence of traveling waves for all values of the diffusion coefficient; (ii) The possibility of a phase transition from a wave to a stationary state for increasing diffusion coefficients; (iii) The possibility of the existence of two traveling waves with different speeds for the same diffusion coefficient; and (iv) The existence of a critical diffusion coefficient for which the two waves coalesce to a single wave.
